claim_verdicts.evidence: refs: "Instead of having business logic depend on data access or other infrastructure concerns, this dependency is inverted: infrastructure and implementation details depend on the Application Core." and "dependencies flow toward the innermost circle... the Application Core has no dependencies on other application layers." Round-1 suggested wording applied; consistent with DonHang.Api -> DonHang.Infrastructure (not out of the core). DonHang.Domain@stage-1 names only its own types and .NET (sole using: System.Security.Cryptography).

refs: "One disadvantage of this traditional layering approach is that compile-time dependencies run from the top to the bottom. That is, the UI layer depends on the BLL, which depends on the DAL. This means that the BLL, which usually holds the most important logic in the application, is dependent on data access implementation details (and often on the existence of a database)."

git show stage-1:DonHang.Infrastructure/DonHang.Infrastructure.csproj → line 11 `<ProjectReference Include="..\DonHang.Domain\DonHang.Domain.csproj" />`, the only ProjectReference. git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/DonHang.Domain.csproj → 10 lines, one PropertyGroup, no ItemGroup. No Directory.Build.props at stage-1; Directory.Packages.props has only PackageVersion items (no GlobalPackageReference).

OrderService.cs@stage-1: `public sealed class OrderService(IOrderRepository repository, INotifier notifier)`; PlaceOrderAsync: `await repository.AddAsync(order); await repository.SaveChangesAsync();`. IOrderRepository.cs: namespace DonHang.Domain, four members FindAsync(int)→Task<Order?>, ListByCustomerAsync(int)→Task<List<Order>>, AddAsync(Order)→Task, SaveChangesAsync()→Task.

EfOrderRepository.cs@stage-1 lines 1-10: `using DonHang.Domain;` `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;` `public sealed class EfOrderRepository(DonHangDbContext db) : IOrderRepository` `public Task<Order?> FindAsync(int id) => db.Orders.Include(o => o.Items).FirstOrDefaultAsync(o => o.Id == id);`

ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:15 `services.AddScoped<IOrderRepository, EfOrderRepository>();`; Program.cs:18-19 `builder.Services.AddDonHangInfrastructure(connectionString); builder.Services.AddScoped<OrderService>();`; OrdersController injects OrderService and Create calls orderService.PlaceOrderAsync.

refs: "Outside of the Application Core, both the UI and the Infrastructure layers depend on the Application Core, but not on one another (necessarily)." and "the UI layer project may need to reference the Infrastructure project... the simplest approach is to allow the UI project to reference the Infrastructure project".

refs line 64: traditional layering makes the BLL "dependent on data access implementation details". OrderService must name the interface it calls; if declared in DonHang.Infrastructure, DonHang.Domain needs a ProjectReference to it, and packages flow through that reference (see claim 13 build: Npgsql/EF Core types usable via the ProjectReference alone).
